title: Dhananjoy Chatterjee @ Dhana v. State of West Bengal
crime_type: Residential Security Guard Breach / Premeditated Rape & Homicide of Schoolgirl
court_or_authority: Supreme Court of India / High Court at Calcutta
source: Supreme Court of India Official Judgment & Indian Kanoon (doc/1359141)
evidence: Stolen wristwatch belonging to victim recovered from suspect rural ancestral home in Bankura district
Duty register confirming suspect was posted as security guard at Anand Apartment on date and time of crime
Severe ligature strangulation marks and multiple blunt head wounds documented in Nil Ratan Sircar Medical College autopsy
Seminal fluid stains and pubic hair forensic match connecting suspect to scene
modus_operandi: Employed as residential building security guard. After victim mother complained to building society regarding his leering behaviour leading to his transfer, he nursed intense vindictive resentment. Monitored the flat until victim was alone, gained forced entry, assaulted, raped, and strangled 14-year-old schoolgirl before stealing her wristwatch to fake burglary.
personality_disorder: Spiteful grievance accumulation, predatory sexual opportunism, and explosive vindictive violence.
common_traits: Insider breach of trust by residential security personnel
Retaliation against domestic tenant harassment complaints
Physical assault followed by clothes ligature strangulation
Theft of minor personal effects to simulate burglary
summary: First judicial execution in India in the 21st century (executed in 2004). Supreme Court held that security guards entrusted with building safety who breach that sacred trust to prey upon defenseless residents fall within the rarest of rare doctrine warranting the death penalty.
